schemes.apiKeyAndSecretKey.description: "HTTP Basic authentication. Username is the project API key, password is the project secret key. Both are found in Amplitude under Settings → Projects → General. Credentials must be base64 encoded.\n\nThis scheme is project-scoped and all-or-nothing: a key pair grants every operation on its project. There is no narrower grant. When an agent needs least-privilege access, prefer the MCP server and its `mcpOAuth` scopes over these keys."

schemes.mcpOAuth.description: "OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE, used by the Amplitude MCP server at `https://mcp.amplitude.com/mcp`.

Endpoints and scopes here mirror the authorization server metadata at https://mcp.amplitude.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, which is authoritative. Clients may be registered dynamically (RFC 7591) at `https://mcp.amplitude.com/register`; public clients are supported.

Scopes bound the token but do not widen it — every call is additionally enforced against the permissions of the Amplitude user who approved the grant. Request the narrowest scope that covers the task.

For EU data residency, substitute `https://mcp.eu.amplitude.com`."
schemes.mcpOAuth.flows.authorizationCode.scopes.["mcp:read"]: "Read charts, dashboards, cohorts, experiments, feature flags, events, properties, and session replays."
schemes.mcpOAuth.flows.authorizationCode.scopes.["mcp:write"]: "Create and modify dashboards, notebooks, experiments, cohorts, and metrics."
schemes.mcpOAuth.flows.authorizationCode.scopes.offline_access: "Issue a refresh token so the agent can act after the user closes the browser. Omit for one-shot interactive tasks."
schemes.orgApiKeyAndSecretKey.description: "DSAR uses HTTP Basic with the org API key and org secret key, as documented in the DSAR request examples."
